identity.title: Exploring Synthesizable Chemical Space with Iterative Pathway Refinements

problem.claim: Molecular generative models may produce molecules without guaranteed synthesizability.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often navigate the exponentially large synthesizable-molecule space poorly and provide limited coverage.

contributions.claim: ReaSyn projects input molecules onto synthesizable space to obtain synthesizable analogs through iterative pathway refinement.
It uses a pathway representation supporting bottom-up and top-down synthetic-tree traversal, sampled by one unified autoregressive model for bidirectional subtree refinement.
It adds discrete flow-based whole-pathway editing through insertion, deletion, and substitution, combined with iterative decoding.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present ReaSyn as an iterative, bidirectional pathway-refinement framework combining unified traversal modeling with discrete holistic pathway editing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ReaSyn attains the highest reconstruction rate and pathway diversity for synthesizable-molecule reconstruction.
The authors report the highest optimization performance in synthesizable goal-directed molecular optimization.
The authors report significant outperformance over previous synthesizable projection methods in synthesizable hit expansion.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies lack of guaranteed synthesizability and poor coverage of existing methods as the central challenge.
ReaSyn projects inputs into synthesizable space using a pathway representation and a unified model for bottom-up and top-down traversal.
Bidirectional subtree refinement is combined with whole-pathway discrete edits in an iterative reasoning cycle.
The authors report leading reconstruction, diversity, optimization, and hit-expansion results relative to prior projection methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a stated search-space limitation with a multi-stage refinement cycle that separately supports local subtree changes and holistic pathway edits.

lessons.interpretation: A useful design pattern is to map a broad failure mode to complementary operations at different structural scales.
lessons.application: For a structured generation task, specify one local refinement operation and one global edit operation, then describe how they form an explicit iteration cycle.
lessons.exception: This pattern may be unsuitable when global edits violate hard validity constraints or when the task has no meaningful hierarchical structure.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical results, datasets, baselines, statistical details, or evaluation conditions for the reported comparisons.
It does not specify how synthesizability, pathway diversity, optimization performance, or hit expansion are operationalized.
The abstract does not establish independently verified correctness, effectiveness, reproducibility, or priority of the claimed novelty.
